content.overview: s. 94 plus Orders XXXVIII, XXXIX and XL: attachment before judgment, temporary injunction, receiver.
content.glance: s. 94 plus Orders XXXVIII, XXXIX and XL: attachment before judgment, temporary injunction, receiver.
content.study:
Introduction
Supplemental proceedings keep the decree from becoming paper. s. 94 lists the powers. The Orders supply the tests.

Order XXXIX
Temporary injunction: prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury. r. 3 — ex parte only with reasons and immediate hearing. r. 2A — disobedience.

Order XXXVIII
Arrest or attachment before judgment if the defendant is about to remove himself or his property to defeat the decree.

Order XL
Receiver when it is just and convenient.

Illustration
Builder raises a wall on disputed land. Neighbour shows title papers and continuing damage. Status quo under Order XXXIX rr. 1–2.

Fail-illustration
Pure money claim, defendant is solvent. Damages are adequate. Injunction is usually refused.

Authority
Dalpat Kumar (1992) 1 SCC 719 — three-fold test.
Morgan Stanley (1994) 4 SCC 225 — ex parte injunction is exceptional.
Manohar Lal Chopra AIR 1962 SC 527 — s. 151 is not a free-standing rival to Order XXXIX.

Close with s. 94 and Order XXXIX CPC, 1908.

cases.name: Dalpat Kumar v. Prahlad Singh
cases.holding: Prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury.

cases.name: Morgan Stanley v. Kartick Das
cases.holding: Ex parte injunction needs reasons and a prompt hearing.

questionsAndAnswers.question: State the tests for a temporary injunction.
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Order XXXIX rr. 1–2. Three-fold test. Notice under r. 3. Dalpat Kumar. Cite Order XXXIX CPC, 1908.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Trial court grants an ex parte injunction without reasons. Advise.
questionsAndAnswers.answer:
Issue. Is the order sustainable?
Rule. r. 3 proviso — reasons and immediate listing. Morgan Stanley.
Application. The order is vulnerable. Move r. 4 or appeal under Order XLIII where it lies.
Conclusion. Order XXXIX rr. 3–4 CPC.

examTips: Never write a final finding of title at the interlocutory stage.
